title: Report a failed engine or tooling probe as unknown, not as missing
body:
## Summary
A failed detect-engines or detect-tooling call reads as "Not found" or as no rows at all.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/useProjectScan.ts:83 and :116 swallow the failure. An engine probe failure writes ok:false "Not found"; a tooling failure yields zero tool rows, and missingRequirements only counts present rows, so missingToolCount drops to 0 and the banner moves on as if the toolchain were fine. Fixed means a third checklist state (unknown) that missingRequirements and deriveNextStep understand.

## Flow
- detect-tooling returns 500
- useProjectScan pushes no tool rows
- missingToolCount is 0 and the banner says Create Project or Build & Verify

## Expected impact
Users on a flaky server stop being told tools are fine or absent when nothing was measured. Risk: ChecklistItem gains a state that toolchain.ts and its tests must read.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a probe failure is distinct from a missing tool
Before: walked: detect-tooling 500 gives 0 tool rows and missingToolCount 0
After: predicted: rows marked unknown and no next step derived from them
Method: simulation - the change crosses src/lib/project-setup/toolchain.ts, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Extend use-project-scan-unreadable.test.tsx with failing detect-engines and detect-tooling replies; assert the unknown state and no derived next step

title: Open in Explorer without spending a CLI agent run
body:
## Summary
Open in Explorer sends a prompt to a Claude CLI session to open one folder.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/ProjectSetupModule.tsx:106 dispatches "Open the folder ... in Windows Explorer." through setupCLI, the session Create Project also uses. A local action needs a server route that launches explorer.exe on a validated path. No such route exists (grep for explorer.exe and open-folder in src: only this call site).

## Flow
- User clicks Open in Explorer
- A CLI session starts and bills a model turn
- The agent shells out to open the folder

## Expected impact
One click stops costing a model turn and stops occupying the setup session. Risk: a new route launching a process needs the same local-path check the browse route uses.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a local action costs no model call
Before: 1 model run per click
After: 0 model runs per click
Method: simulation - needs a new API route outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Route test asserting checkLocalPath rejection and spawn of explorer on a valid path; module test asserting no sendPrompt on click

title: Make the Build Files check look for build files
body:
## Summary
The Build Files row passes on any subfolder of Source/.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/useProjectScan.ts:182 sets hasBuildFiles from sourceData.directories.length > 0. A Source/ holding only an empty folder reports "Build files found", though no Target.cs or Build.cs exists. The list action returns directories and .uproject files only, so a real check needs the route to report them.

## Flow
- Source/ contains an empty Foo/ folder
- list returns directories [Foo]
- Checklist shows Build files found

## Expected impact
The checklist stops claiming build files it never looked at. Risk: projects with unusual layouts could flip to failing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the row reports what it names
Before: Empty Source/Foo reads as ok:true
After: Same input reads as ok:false
Method: simulation - needs the browse route to return Target.cs/Build.cs presence
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: Route test on a temp tree with and without Target.cs; hook test on both replies

title: Say so when Build & Verify falls back to a different engine
body:
## Summary
With no installed engine matching the project, the prompt silently uses the first one.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/prompts.ts:49 falls back to engines[0], the newest install, so a 5.7 project is compiled by 5.8 under a prompt titled "UE 5.7 project". Nothing in the panel or the prompt says the engines differ, while the wizard does warn about engine fit through engineFitNote.

## Flow
- Project records 5.7, only 5.8 is installed
- Build & Verify runs against UE_5.8
- The report reads as a 5.7 verification

## Expected impact
A green build stops implying the recorded engine was tested. Risk: wording only if kept to a warning; refusing to build would be a product decision.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the verified engine is stated
Before: Mismatch stated in 0 of 1 surfaces
After: Mismatch stated in the prompt and panel
Method: simulation - the wanted behaviour (warn or refuse) is unsettled, so no figure was taken
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: build-verify-prompt.test.ts case with no matching engine asserting the mismatch line

title: Derive the Build & Verify .NET check from the toolchain table
body:
## Summary
The build prompt hard-codes .NET 8 beside the table that declares it.

## Description
src/lib/project-setup/toolchain.ts calls itself the ONE declaration of requirements, and src/components/modules/project-setup/prompts.ts:59 and :63 repeat "8.x" by hand. A runtime bump in the table leaves the prompt blocking on the old version.

## Flow
- TOOLCHAIN dotnet row moves to a new major
- Prompt still stops on no .NET 8.x

## Expected impact
One edit moves both. Risk: the prompt text changes shape if the table gains a version field.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the requirement
Before: 2 hand-written version sites in prompts.ts
After: 0 hand-written sites
Method: simulation - needs a version field on the table, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Prompt test asserting the version comes from the TOOLCHAIN row

title: Remove the unreachable empty state from ProjectFilesPanel
body:
## Summary
The panel draws a "No files created yet" state its only caller never allows.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/ProjectSetupModule.tsx:261 renders the panel only when projectFiles.length > 0, and it is the one consumer (grep ProjectFilesPanel in src: 1 import). src/components/modules/project-setup/ProjectFilesPanel.tsx:33 therefore never renders. Either remove the branch or drop the caller's length check if the empty copy is wanted.

## Flow
- Caller gates on length > 0
- Empty branch cannot render

## Expected impact
About 10 fewer lines, or a reachable empty state. Risk: none beyond the choice of which side to keep.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no unreachable UI
Before: 1 unreachable branch
After: 0 unreachable branches
Method: simulation - which side to keep is a small product call
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Render test of the chosen behaviour for an empty projectFiles

title: Give project-setup a real CLI module id
body:
## Summary
The three CLI sessions cast their module id through unknown.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/ProjectSetupModule.tsx:37, :45 and :53 use 'project-setup' as unknown as SubModuleId, so analytics and prompts attribute runs to an id the union does not contain. Fixed means widening the option type or adding the id, which lives outside this context.

## Flow
- useModuleCLI takes moduleId: SubModuleId
- project-setup is not a member
- The cast hides it at 3 sites

## Expected impact
The compiler checks these runs again. Risk: adding the id can surface exhaustive switches over SubModuleId.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no forced casts
Before: 3 double casts
After: 0 casts
Method: simulation - the type lives in src/types/modules, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Decide the wizard engine hint and the product name it shows
body:
## Summary
The first-run wizard shows a hint with no action behind it and a product name that differs from the docs.

## Description
src/components/modules/project-setup/SetupWizard.tsx:253 reads "Web search for UE 5.8 API changes", which describes nothing the screen does. src/components/modules/project-setup/SetupWizard.tsx:204 expands POF as "Power of Fun", while .claude/CLAUDE.md names the product Pillars of Fortune. Which name is right, and what the hint should say, is the owner's call.

## Flow
- A new user opens the wizard
- Reads a hint with no matching control and a name the docs do not use

## Expected impact
First-run copy matches the product. Risk: none in code.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - first-run copy is accurate
Before: 2 unexplained strings
After: owner decision
Method: simulation - naming is a product decision no instrument can settle
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: Owner decides the name and the hint text
